headline: Personal Agent Protocol (PAP) aims to standardize AI agent interactions with companies
summary: A new open protocol, led by Sierra and Meta, defines how personal AI agents can securely interact with company APIs and services on behalf of users.
details: The Personal Agent Protocol (PAP), nicknamed Poppy, is a new open standard designed to govern how a user's AI agent interacts with companies. It allows agents to sign in as the user, utilize company APIs, join website sessions, and communicate with a company's own AI.

Draft 0.1 of the protocol was published on October 9, 2026, with 35 design partners including major players like OpenAI, Visa, Mastercard, and PayPal. The core of the protocol relies on a discovery file located at /.well-known/poppy.json.

This poppy.json file, served over HTTPS, acts as the central configuration document. It specifies the protocol version, the organization details, and the authentication issuer. Crucially, it also lists the APIs the agent is authorized to use.

However, a valid-looking poppy.json is not enough for security. A personal agent must also fetch the OAuth server metadata from the specified issuer and verify that the issuer is indeed the expected sign-in server. This prevents malicious sites from redirecting agents to fake authentication pages.

As of October 11, 2026, none of the launch or design partners, including giants like Meta, Visa, and OpenAI, were serving a functional poppy.json file. The only live files observed were developer demos, indicating that the first company to correctly implement the protocol will be easily identifiable.

To help developers and companies check their compliance, a tool called PAP Checker has been developed. It independently verifies a domain's poppy.json file against the draft 0.1 specifications, checking for valid JSON structure, HTTPS compliance, and correct OAuth server metadata publication.
